textoOriginal: The 1H-tautomer of pyrazole.
A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is joined only to a single oxygen. It is a colourless, odourless, tasteless, toxic gas.
A benzoquinone resulting from the formal oxidation of catechol.
A purine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside having adenine as the nucleobase.
The 7H-tautomer of purine.
A 17-oxo steroid that is estra-1,3,5(10)-triene substituted by an hydroxy group at position 3 and an oxo group at position 17.
A phosphoamino acid consisting of creatine having a phospho group attached at the primary nitrogen of the guanidino group.
A primary arylamine in which an amino functional group is substituted for one of the benzene hydrogens.
A chlorocarbon that is tetrachloro substituted ethene.
A glycosylglucose consisting of two D-glucopyranose units connected by an α-(1→4)-linkage.
A retinol in which all four exocyclic double bonds have E- (trans-) geometry.
An androstanoid having 17β-hydroxy and 3-oxo groups, together with unsaturation at C-4‒C-5..
An octadecadienoic acid in which the two double bonds are at positions 9 and 12 and have Z (cis) stereochemistry.
A pyrimidine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate having cytosine as the nucleobase.
The simplest member of the quinoline class of compounds, comprising a benzene ring ortho fused to C-2 and C-3 of a pyridine ring.
A purine nucleobase that consists of purine bearing an oxo substituent at position 6.
A dicarboxylic acid that is pyrole bearing aminomethyl, carboxymethyl and 2-carboxyethyl substituents at positions 2, 3 and 4 respectively.
A myo-inositol hexakisphosphate in which each hydroxy group of myo-inositol is monophosphorylated.
A straight-chain saturated fatty acid containing five carbon atoms.
A methyl sulfide in which the sulfur atom is substituted by two methyl groups. It is produced naturally by some marine algae.
A 2-hydroxy monocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid where the methyl group has been hydroxylated.
A purine ribonucleoside 5'-diphosphate resulting from the formal condensation of the hydroxy group at the 5' position of guanosine with pyrophosphoric acid.
A pyrimidine nucleoside in which cytosine is attached to ribofuranose via a β-N^(1)-glycosidic bond.

A common and naturally occurring pyrimidine nucleobase in which the pyrimidine ring is substituted with two oxo groups at positions 2 and 4. Found in RNA, it base pairs with adenine and replaces thymine during DNA transcription.
The simplest member of the class toluenes consisting of a benzene core which bears a single methyl substituent.
A cyclic carotene obtained by dimerisation of all-trans-retinol. A strongly-coloured red-orange pigment abundant in plants and fruit and the most active and important provitamin A carotenoid.
A monoterpenoid that is octa-1,6-diene substituted by methyl groups at positions 3 and 7 and a hydroxy group at position 3. It has been isolated from plants like Ocimum canum.
A straight chain alkane composed of 8 carbon atoms.

A 2'-deoxycytidine having geminal fluoro substituents in the 2'-position. An inhibitor of ribonucleotide reductase, gemcitabine is used in the treatment of various carcinomas, particularly non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic cancer, bladder cancer and breast cancer.
A benzenediol comprising benzene core carrying two hydroxy substituents para to each other.
A hydroxybenzaldehyde that is benzaldehyde substituted with a hydroxy group at position C-4.
An amino phenol (one of the three possible isomers) which has the single amino substituent located para to the phenolic -OH group.
Molecule comprising two covalently bonded iodine atoms with overall zero charge..
A chlorophenol that is phenol substituted by 5 chloro groups.

A 17α-hydroxy-C₂₁-steroid that is pregn-4-ene substituted by oxo groups at positions 3 and 20 and hydroxy groups at positions 11, 17 and 21. Cortisol is a corticosteroid hormone or glucocorticoid produced by zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex, which is a part of the adrenal gland. It is usually referred to as the "stress hormone" as it is involved in response to stress and anxiety, controlled by corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH). It increases blood pressure and blood sugar, and reduces immune responses.
An inorganic sodium salt composed of a sodium cation and an azanide anion. It is used as a strong base in organic synthesis.
A 3-(1-methylpyrrolidin-2-yl)pyridine in which the chiral centre has S-configuration. The naturally occurring and most active enantiomer of nicotine, isolated from Nicotiana tabacum.
An organochlorine compound that is dichloro-substituted acetamide containing a nitrobenzene ring, an amide bond and two alcohol functions.
An oxopurine in which the purine ring is substituted by oxo groups at positions 2 and 6 and N-9 is protonated.
A member of the class of formamides that is formamide in which the amino hydrogens are replaced by methyl groups.
A pyrimidine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside having thymine as the nucleobase.
A triol with a structure of propane substituted at positions 1, 2 and 3 by hydroxy groups.
An oxopurine in which the purine ring is substituted by oxo groups at positions 2, 6, and 8.
The primary alcohol that is the simplest aliphatic alcohol, comprising a methyl and an alcohol group.
The acyclic form of D-ribose 5-phosphate.
A pyrimidine nucleobase that is uracil in which the hydrogen at position 5 is replaced by a methyl group.
A secondary alcohol that is propane in which one of the hydrogens attached to the central carbon is substituted by a hydroxy group.
An aminobiphenyl that is biphenyl substituted by an amino group at position 4.
A member of the class of hydroxyindoles that is 1H-indole substituted by a hydroxy group at position 3.
A cyclic ketone that consists of cyclohexane bearing a single oxo substituent.
An α,ω-dicarboxylic acid that is a linear five-carbon dicarboxylic acid.
A mononuclear parent hydride consisting of covalently bonded hydrogen and chlorine atoms.
An indolyl alcohol that is ethanol substituted by a 1H-indol-3-yl group at position 2.
An optically active form of tyrosine having L-configuration.
A ε-lactone that is oxepane substituted by an oxo group at position 2.
The D-enantiomer of glucitol (also known as D-sorbitol).
A saturated fatty aldehyde formally arising from reduction of the carboxy group of caprylic acid (octanoic acid).
A tetrahydropyridine that is 1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine substituted by a methyl group at position 1 and a phenyl group at position 4.
A carbamate ester obtained by the formal condensation of ethanol with carbamic acid. It has been found in alcoholic beverages.
An aromatic alcohol that consists of benzene bearing a single hydroxymethyl substituent.
A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.
An elemental molecule consisting of two trivalently-bonded nitrogen atoms.
A butenedioic acid in which the C=C double bond has E geometry. It is an intermediate metabolite in the citric acid cycle.
An L-α-amino acid; the L-isomer of lysine.
An azacycloalkane that is cyclohexane in which one of the carbons is replaced by a nitrogen. It is a metabolite of cadaverine, a polyamine found in the human intestine.
An optically active form of glutamine having L-configuration.
A member of the class of phylloquinones that consists of 1,4-naphthoquinone having methyl and phytyl groups at positions 2 and 3 respectively. The parent of the class of phylloquinones.

A dihydropyridine that is 1,4-dihydropyridine substituted by a methyl, {2-[benzyl(methyl)amino]ethoxy}carbonyl, 3-nitrophenyl, methoxycarbonyl and methyl groups at positions 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, respectively.
An alcohol that consists of cyclohexane bearing a single hydroxy substituent. The parent of the class of cyclohexanols.
An iminium betaine that is the conjugate base of N-methylnicotinic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.

An alkane-α,ω-diamine comprising a straight-chain pentane core with amino substitutents at positions 1 and 5. A colourless syrupy liquid diamine with a distinctive unpleasant odour, it is a homologue of putresceine and is formed by the bacterial decarboxylation of lysine that occurs during protein hydrolysis during putrefaction of animal tissue. It is also found in plants such as soyabean.
A benzenediol comprising of a benzene core carrying two hydroxy substituents ortho to each other.
A tertiary amine that is ammonia in which each hydrogen atom is substituted by an methyl group.
An α-tocopherol that has R,R,R configuration. The naturally occurring stereoisomer of α-tocopherol, it is found particularly in sunflower and olive oils.
A penicillin in which the substituent at position 6 of the penam ring is a phenylacetamido group.
An arsenic oxoacid comprising one oxo group and three hydroxy groups attached to a central arsenic atom.
Catechol in which the hydrogen at position 4 is substituted by a 2-aminoethyl group.

An iodothyronine compound having iodo substituents at the 3-, 3'- and 5-positions. Although some is produced in the thyroid, most of the 3,3',5-triiodo-L-thyronine in the body is generated by mono-deiodination of L-thyroxine in the peripheral tissues. Its metabolic activity is about 3 to 5 times that of L-thyroxine. The sodium salt is used in the treatment of hypothyroidism.
An elemental molecule consisting of two hydrogens joined by a single bond.
A member of the class of imidazoles that is 1H-imidazole substituted at position C-4 by a 2-aminoethyl group.
A butenedioic acid in which the double bond has cis- (Z)-configuration.
A α,β-unsaturated monocarboxylic acid that is ethene substituted by a carboxy group.
An organophosphorus compound that is phosphane in which the three hydrogens are replaced by methoxy groups. It is an alkylating agent used primarily in the synthesis of organophosphate compounds.
A member of the class of tertiary phosphines that is phosphane in which the three hydrogens are replaced by phenyl groups.
A quinolinemonocarboxylic acid that is quinoline-2-carboxylic acid substituted by a hydroxy group at C-4.
A member of the class of benzaldehydes carrying methoxy and hydroxy substituents at positions 3 and 4 respectively.
The R-enantiomer of noradrenaline.
A phenylethylamine having the phenyl substituent at the 2-position.
The monophosphate ester obtained by condensation of phosphoric acid with the primary hydroxy group of pyridoxal.
A one-carbon compound consisting of a methine group triple bonded to a nitrogen atom
A phenol substituted at position 4 by a 2-hydroxyethyl group.
A member of the class of hydrazines that is hydrazine substituted by two methyl groups at position 1.
A molecule whose structure comprises two phenyl rings linked by a N=N double bond; the parent compound of the azobenzene class of compounds.
An inorganic carbonate salt of barium.
An inorganic nitrate salt of barium.
An organic calcium salt composed of calcium cations and citrate anions in a 3:2 ratio.
A tautomer of pyrrole that has the double bonds at positions 2 and 4.
A zwitterion formed from ciprofloxacin by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group; major species at pH 7.3.
A zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of 4-aminobenzoic acid.

An artemisinin derivative that is artemisinin in which the lactone has been converted to the corresponding lactol methyl ether. It is used in combination with lumefantrine as an antimalarial for the treatment of multi-drug resistant strains of falciparum malaria.
A methyl ketone that is butane substituted by an oxo group at position 2 and two methyl groups at position 3.
A chloroaniline in which the chloro atom is para to the aniline amino group.
A furan bearing a hydroxymethyl substituent at the 2-position.
A tricarboxylic acid that is prop-1-ene substituted by carboxy groups at positions 1, 2 and 3.
A sesquiterpene lactone obtained from sweet wormwood, Artemisia annua, which is used as an antimalarial for the treatment of multi-drug resistant strains of falciparum malaria.
An ammonium salt that is the diammonium salt of carbonic acid.
A pentene with unsaturation at position 1.
An inorganic nitrate salt having Al(3+) as the counterion.
A titanium molecular entity that is titanium which carries 4 chlorine atoms.
An inorganic potassium salt of permanganic acid.
An inorganic nitrate salt having zinc(2+) as the couterion.
The organic ammonium salt of thiocyanic acid.
A metal sulfate compound having copper(2+) as the metal ion.
A cycloalkane that consists of five carbons each bonded with two hydrogens above and below the plane. The parent of the class of cyclopentanes.
An ether that is the 2-acetyl-4-(butanoylamino)phenyl ether of the primary hydroxy group of 3-(propan-2-ylamino)propane-1,2-diol.
An oxopurine that is guanine substituted by a (2-hydroxyethoxy)methyl substituent at position 9. Used in the treatment of viral infections.

An N-nitro compound that is 1,3,5-triazinane in which all three of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogens have been replaced by nitro groups. It is widely used in both industrial and military explosives.
An alkene that is hexane carrying a double bond at position 1.
A chlorine oxoacid with formula HOCl; a weak, unstable acid, it is the active form of chlorine in water.

A monocarboxylic acid amide that is the 2-(diethylamino)ethyl amide of 2-butoxyquinoline-4-carboxylic acid. One of the most potent and toxic of the long-acting local anesthetics, its parenteral use was restricted to spinal anesthesia. It is now generally only used (usually as the hydrochloride) in creams and ointments and in suppositories for temporary relief of pain and itching associated with skin and anorectal conditions.
Any secondary alcohol that is one of the eight possible diastereoisomers of 5-methyl-2-(propan-2-yl)cyclohexan-1-ol.
An α,β-unsaturated monocarboxylic acid that is acrylic acid in which the hydrogen at position 2 is substituted by a methyl group.
A pyrido[4,3-b]indole compound having a 5-methyl-1H-imidazol-4-ylmethyl group at the 2-position.

A member of the class of phenylethanolamines that is 4-(2-amino-1-hydroxyethyl)-2-(hydroxymethyl)phenol having a tert-butyl group attached to the nirogen atom. It acts as a β-adrenergic agonist used in the treatment of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

The oxime carbamate resulting from the addition of 2-methyl-2-(methylsulfanyl)propanaldoxime to methyl isocyanate. A member of the class of oxime carbamate insecticides, aldicarb is a mixture of E and Z isomers; it is not known which isomer is more active.
A 1,1-bis(phosphonic acid) that is methanebis(phosphonic acid) in which the two methylene hydrogens are replaced by hydroxy and 3-aminopropyl groups.

A member of the class of piperidines that is piperidine having a 2-(4-ethyl-5-oxo-4,5-dihydro-1H-tetrazol-1-yl)ethyl group at the 1-position as well as N-phenylpropanamido- and methoxymethyl groups at the 4-position.

An elemental molecule with formula O₃. An explosive, pale blue gas (b.p. −112°C) that has a characteristic, pungent odour, it is continuously produced in the upper atmosphere by the action of solar ultraviolet radiation on atmospheric oxygen. It is an antimicrobial agent used in the production of bottled water, as well as in the treatment of meat, poultry and other foodstuffs.
A dimethylxanthine having the two methyl groups located at positions 1 and 7. It is a metabolite of caffeine and theobromine in animals.

A pentaerythritol nitrate in which all four hydroxy groups of pentaerythritol have been converted to the corresponding nitrate ester. It is a vasodilator with properties similar to those of glyceryl trinitrate, but with a more prolonged duration of action, and is used for treatment of angina pectoris. It is also one of the most powerful high explosives known and is a component of the plastic explosive known as Semtex.
A nitrile that is acetonitrile where one of the methyl hydrogens is substituted by a phenyl group.
A phosphorus oxoacid that consists of one oxo and three hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central phosphorus atom.

A member of the class of triazolobenzodiazepines that is 4H-[1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-a][1,4]benzodiazepine carrying methyl, phenyl and chloro substituents at positions 1, 6 and 8 respectively. Alprazolam is only found in individuals that have taken this drug.
A member of the class of adamantanes that is used as an antiviral and antiparkinson drug.
A nitrile that is acrylonitrile in which the carbon-carbon double bond has been reduced to a single bond.
An amino cyclitol glycoside that is kanamycin A acylated at the N-1 position by a 4-amino-2-hydroxybutyryl group.
A member of the class of pyrazines resulting from the formal monoacylation of guanidine with the carboxy group of 3,5-diamino-6-chloropyrazine-2-carboxylic acid.

A member of the class of 1-benzofurans that is 1-benzofuran substituted by a butyl group at position 2 and a 4-[2-(diethylamino)ethoxy]-3,5-diiodobenzoyl group at position 3. It is a cardiovascular drug used for the treatment of cardiac dysrhythmias.
A tertiary amino compound that is 1,3,5-triazapenta-1,4-diene substituted by a methyl group at position 3 and 2,4-dimethylphenyl groups at positions 1 and 5.
An organic tricyclic compound that is 10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d][7]annulene substituted by a 3-(dimethylamino)propylidene group at position 5.
An inorganic sodium salt having hydrogensulfite as the counterion.
An inorganic chloride salt having sodium(1+) as the counterion.

A member of the class of barbiturates that is pyrimidine-2,4,6(1H,3H,5H)-trione substituted by a 3-methylbutyl and an ethyl group at position 5. Amobarbital has been shown to exhibit sedative and hypnotic properties.
A quinoline having a chloro group at the 7-position and an aryl amino group at the 4-position.
A dibenzooxazepine compound having a chloro substituent at the 2-position and a piperazin-1-yl group at the 11-position.
A penicillin in which the substituent at position 6 of the penam ring is a 2-amino-2-(4-hydroxyphenyl)acetamido group.
A sulfur oxoacid that consists of two oxo and two hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central sulfur atom.
A nitrite ester having isopentyl as the alkyl group.
A cyclic ether that is butane in which one hydrogen from each methyl group is substituted by an oxygen.
A 1,2,4-triazole compound having a 3,5-bis(2-cyano-2-propyl)benzyl group at the 1-position.
A tertiary amine that is ethanolamine having two N-methyl substituents.
A monomethoxybenzene that is methoxybenzene substituted by a prop-1-en-1-yl group at position 4.
An alkanesulfonic acid in which the alkyl group directly linked to the sulfo functionality is methyl.
A chlorocarbon that is methane in which all the hydrogens have been replaced by chloro groups.
A xylene with methyl groups at positions 1 and 4.
The parent structure of the family of 1,4-naphthoquinones, in which the oxo groups of the quinone moiety are at positions 1 and 4 of the naphthalene ring. Derivatives have pharmacological properties.
A 17β-hydroxy steroid that is testosterone bearing a methyl group at the 17α position.
A penicillin compound having a 6β-(phenoxyacetyl)amino side-chain.
A vinylarene that is benzene carrying a vinyl group. It has been isolated from the benzoin resin produced by Styrax species.

An N-acyl-amino acid that is a form of the water-soluble vitamin B₉. Its biologically active forms (tetrahydrofolate and others) are essential for nucleotide biosynthesis and homocysteine remethylation.
An aminobenzenesulfonic acid that is aniline sulfonated at the para-position.
An indoledione that is the 2,3-diketo derivative of indole.
A pyrimidine that is a derivative of cytosine, having a methyl group at the 5-position.
A saturated organic heteromonocyclic parent that is a three-membered heterocycle of two carbon atoms and one oxygen atom.
An aminobenzoic acid that is salicylic acid substituted by an amino group at position 4.

A pregnane-based steroidal hormone produced by the outer-section (zona glomerulosa) of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland, and acts on the distal tubules and collecting ducts of the kidney to cause the conservation of sodium, secretion of potassium, increased water retention, and increased blood pressure. The overall effect of aldosterone is to increase reabsorption of ions and water in the kidney.
The D-enantiomer of psicose.
A phenol that is a natural monoterpene derivative of cymene.
The simplest member of the class of psoralens that is 7H-furo[3,2-g]chromene having a keto group at position 7. It has been found in plants like Psoralea corylifolia and Ficus salicifolia.
A methyl ketone that is acetone in which one of the methyl groups has been replaced by a phenyl group.

A dicarboximide that is 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperidine-2,6-dione in which one of the hydrogens attached to the carbon bearing the hydroxy group is replaced by a 3,5-dimethyl-2-oxocyclohexyl group. It is an antibiotic produced by the bacterium Streptomyces griseus.
An ether having methyl and tert-butyl as the two alkyl components.

A pyranoindolizinoquinoline that is pyrano[3',4':6,7]indolizino[1,2-b]quinoline which is substituted by oxo groups at positions 3 and 14, and by an ethyl group and a hydroxy group at position 4 (the S enantiomer).
An ethyl sulfide compound having two ethyl groups attached to a sulfur atom.
A trimethylxanthine in which the three methyl groups are located at positions 1, 3, and 7. A purine alkaloid that occurs naturally in tea and coffee.

A phosphonic acid resulting from the formal oxidative coupling of the methyl group of methylphosphonic acid with the amino group of glycine. It is one of the most commonly used herbicides worldwide, and the only one to target the enzyme 5-enolpyruvyl-3-shikimate phosphate synthase (EPSPS).
The acetate ester formed between acetic acid and ethanol.
A member of the class of chloroethanes substituted by two chloro groups at positions 1 and 2.
A nitroarene consisting of benzene carrying a single nitro substituent. An industrial chemical used widely in the production of aniline.
A benzenediol that is benzene dihydroxylated at positions 1 and 3.
An arenesulfonic acid that is benzenesulfonic acid in which the hydrogen at position 4 is replaced by a methyl group.
The sodium salt of hydrogen azide (hydrazoic acid).
A chlorocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid carrying a 2-chloro substituent.
A naphthylamine carrying the amino group at position 2.

A colchicine that has (S)-configuration. It is a secondary metabolite, has anti-inflammatory properties and is used to treat gout, crystal-induced joint inflammation, familial Mediterranean fever, and many other conditions.
A chlorophenoxyacetic acid that is phenoxyacetic acid in which the ring hydrogens at postions 2, 4 and 5 are substituted by chlorines.
The D-enantiomer of erythrose.
A trioxane that is 1,3,5-trioxane substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 4 and 6.
A trimer of cyanamide, with a 1,3,5-triazine skeleton.
A phenylhydrazine that is the monophenyl derivative of hydrazine.
A 3-hydroxy steroid that is estra-1,3,5(10)-trien-3-ol substituted by additional hydroxy groups at positions 16 and 17 (16α,17β-stereoisomer).
A nitroso compound that is the nitroso derivative of benzene; a diamagnetic hybrid of singlet O₂ and azobenzene.
A nitrile that is hydrogen cyanide in which the hydrogen has been replaced by a phenyl group.

A complex glycopeptide from Streptomyces orientalis. It inhibits a specific step in the synthesis of the peptidoglycan layer in the Gram-positive bacteria Staphylococcus aureus and Clostridium difficile.
An N-acetyl-D-glucosamine having β-configuration at the anomeric centre.
A D-fructofuranose 1,6-bisphosphate with a β-configuration at the anomeric position.
A cresol that is phenol substituted by a methyl group at position 2. It is a minor urinary metabolite of toluene.
A xylene substituted by methyl groups at positions 1 and 2.
The simplest member of the class of monochlorobenzenes, that is benzene in which a single hydrogen has been substituted by a chlorine.
A member of the class of ethanolamines that is ethanolamine having a N-hydroxyethyl substituent.
